in_text_mentions: substantial extracalvarial hypodense collection measuring 15 x 12 x 6.5 cm in the bilateral frontoparietal and left temporal regions, with an approximate volume of 1300 milliliters (Figure 3, Figure 4). Ultrasound-guided aspiration confirmed the presence of a hematoma in the subgaleal space, with the aspirate exhibiting a bloody consistency. Angiograms of the bilateral internal carotid and vertebral arteries showed normal results. panels.rationale: The ultrasound image clearly displays an anechoic fluid collection that spans the suture line, which is the definition of a subgaleal hemorrhage, confirming the diagnosis presented in the caption and in-text.

panels.figure_caption: Point-of-care ultrasound demonstrating a subgaleal hematoma (*) that is seen to cross over the suture line (arrow).
in_text_mentions: A linear, high-frequency transducer was used to obtain both sets of images. The first patient had a POCUS examination that revealed an anechoic fluid collection that did not cross the sagittal suture. These findings were consistent with a cephalohematoma (Image 1). The second patient had a POCUS examination that demonstrated an anechoic fluid collection that crossed over the sagittal suture. These findings were consistent with a subgaleal hematoma (Image 2).
